name: Phoenix
operatingHours: Valley Metro Rail (A and B lines) runs ~4:00 AM–~midnight daily, every ~12–20 min, with later trains (~2:00 AM) on Friday and Saturday nights. The Tempe Streetcar runs ~5:00 AM–~11:00 PM (shorter hours on Sundays). PHX Sky Train runs 24 h, every ~3–5 min.
fareInfo: Light rail and buses: $2 per ride, $4 for a 1-day pass (2026). Tap a Copper card or the Valley Metro app and fares cap at $4/day, $20/week and $64/month; paper tickets from platform machines. Tempe Streetcar: $1 per 45-minute ride, counted toward the same caps. PHX Sky Train is free.

lines.name: Tempe Streetcar
stations: Tempe Beach Park / Rio Salado Pkwy

sights.name: Desert Botanical Garden
sights.note: Fifty-plus acres of cacti, agaves and desert wildflowers on looping trails among the red buttes of Papago Park.
sights.hours: Daily from 7:00 AM; usually closes ~8:00 PM (to 10:00 PM on event nights)

sights.name: Musical Instrument Museum
sights.note: Thousands of instruments from every country, with headsets that play each exhibit as you walk up; far north Phoenix, no rail link.

sights.name: Camelback Mountain
sights.note: Phoenix's signature peak: a steep, rocky scramble to the summit via the Echo Canyon or Cholla trails. Start early and carry plenty of water.
sights.hours: Trails sunrise–sunset; trailhead lots fill early

sights.name: Heard Museum
sights.note: A leading museum of American Indian art and cultures, with Hopi katsina dolls, jewelry and a courtyard café.

sights.name: Hole in the Rock
sights.note: A short climb to a wind-carved opening in a red sandstone butte, framing a classic sunset view over the city.
sights.hours: Papago Park ~5:00 AM–11:00 PM daily; free

sights.name: Phoenix Zoo
sights.note: A large non-profit zoo in Papago Park with an Arizona desert trail, orangutans and a giraffe feeding deck.
sights.hours: 9:00 AM–4:00 PM daily (hours shift seasonally; ZooLights evenings in winter)

sights.name: Chase Field
sights.note: Home of the Arizona Diamondbacks, with a retractable roof, air conditioning and a pool beyond the outfield wall.
sights.hours: MLB game days late Mar–Sep; ballpark tours on select days

sights.name: Phoenix Art Museum
sights.note: The Southwest's largest art museum, spanning Western American, Asian, fashion and modern collections plus miniature period rooms.
sights.hours: Wed & Fri 10:00 AM–8:00 PM, Thu & Sat 10:00 AM–5:00 PM, Sun noon–5:00 PM; closed Mon–Tue

sights.name: South Mountain Park and Preserve
sights.note: One of the largest city parks in the US, with desert trails, petroglyphs and the drive up to Dobbins Lookout for a panorama of the Valley.
sights.hours: Trails 5:00 AM–11:00 PM; roads and lots 5:00 AM–7:00 PM

sights.name: Wrigley Mansion
sights.note: A 1930s hilltop mansion built by chewing-gum magnate William Wrigley Jr., now known for guided tours and its restaurant with city views.
sights.hours: Tours and dining by reservation; hours vary

sights.name: Children's Museum of Phoenix
sights.note: Three floors of hands-on play for kids up to about age ten, inside a restored 1913 schoolhouse downtown.

sights.name: Hall of Flame Museum of Firefighting
sights.note: Hundreds of fire engines, from hand-pulled pumpers to modern rigs, plus a memorial to fallen firefighters.
sights.hours: Tue–Sat 10:00 AM–6:00 PM (last entry 5:00 PM); closed Sun–Mon

sights.name: Piestewa Peak
sights.note: A popular, steep summit trail in the Phoenix Mountains Preserve with 360-degree views across the city.
sights.hours: Trails 5:00 AM–11:00 PM; parking 5:00 AM–7:00 PM

sights.name: St. Mary's Basilica
sights.note: Phoenix's oldest Catholic parish, a 1914 Mission Revival church with large stained-glass windows, visited by Pope John Paul II in 1987.
sights.hours: Open daily for Mass and visits; hours vary

sights.name: Rosson House Museum
sights.note: A restored 1895 Victorian house in Heritage Square, shown on guided tours of early Phoenix life.

sights.name: Arizona Science Center
sights.note: Interactive science exhibits, a planetarium and a giant-screen theater, next to Heritage Square downtown.
sights.hours: Tue–Sun 10:30 AM–4:00 PM; open select Mondays

sights.name: Tempe Town Lake
sights.note: A lake on the Salt River beside Tempe Beach Park, with paths, boat rentals and sunset views, a short walk from the streetcar.
sights.hours: Paths open daily; Tempe Beach Park ~5:00 AM–midnight

sights.name: Roosevelt Row
sights.note: Downtown Phoenix's walkable arts district of murals, galleries, bars and small restaurants, liveliest on First Friday evenings.
sights.hours: Street open 24 h; First Fridays ~6:00–10:00 PM

airports.name: Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport
airports.transitNote: Free PHX Sky Train (on the map) from Terminals 3 and 4 to the 44th St/Washington light rail station in ~5–10 min, then the A Line to downtown Phoenix (~15–20 min) or downtown Tempe (~15 min); $2 ride. Taxi/rideshare to downtown ~15 min.
airports.hours: Sky Train 24 h. Light rail from 44th St: first ~4:00 AM, last ~midnight (~2:00 AM Fri & Sat nights).
